_comment: Hand-curated names and notes for what the game leaves numbered. Never generated; see CLAUDE.md. `kinds` names the block kinds, which the lattice's style values and the records' kind word share. `types` names what stands on a face: `by` names the field whose value tells a type's variants apart, each with its own name and, where it has one, colour and points; `facing` names the field that holds the way a thing points, as quarter turns on its face; `state` names the field that says whether a device a switch toggles starts on; and `points` is what collecting one scores. On a kind or a type, `hazard` marks one that can cost the ball its life, and `fields` says what a raw field holds, by its number, where that is settled; a `facing` or `state` field is named by its key. `levels` is keyed by pack path and index; a level's `score` is the most it scores where the disc holds more than can be collected, and its note says what is out of reach.

1.name: Fire block
1.note: A block whose every face is fire. Touching it swells the ball until it burns or reaches cooler ground.

2.name: Ice block
2.note: A block the ball slides across without stopping until it reaches a normal square or the edge.

3.name: Invisible block
3.note: A block that cannot be seen until the ball is close, or on some levels only from far away. Sunglasses reveal it for a while.

4.name: Acid block
4.note: A green block painted with an acid splat, found only on the object catalogue level. Touching it melts the ball.

5.name: Moving platform
5.note: A platform that travels back and forth along a straight run, stopping briefly at each end.

6.name: Crumbling block
6.note: A block that disappears once rolled onto, leaving time for one move.

7.name: Vanishing block
7.note: A block that fades in and out of existence on a cycle.

8.name: Laser
8.note: A laser beam between two blocks. It burns the ball on touch. A switch of the same colour turns it on and off.

9.name: Level settings
9.note: Not a block but the level's settings, kept where a block would be, often on an empty cell. They say whether the level is a hidden one. On a few levels they also let invisible blocks show from far away and fade as the ball comes near.

666.name: Camera
666.note: Where the level's camera looks, and from what angles, with the level's time.

1.name: Fire
1.note: Fire on one face of an otherwise normal block, which swells the ball until it burns or reaches cooler ground.

2.name: Ice
2.note: Ice on one face of an otherwise normal block.

5.name: Teleporter
5.note: Rolling onto one carries the ball to another of the same colour. A switch of that colour turns them on and off.

7.name: Exit
7.note: Red until every key is collected, then green. Touching it ends the level.

8.name: Clock
8.note: A square that freezes the timer while the ball sits on it.

9.name: Switch
9.note: A button that turns every laser and teleporter of its colour on and off.

10.name: Boost button
10.note: Launches the ball three squares forward, or two forward and one up.

11.name: Moving spikes
11.note: Spikes that rise and retract in turn. They are safe to roll over when down.

12.name: Spikes
12.note: Pops the ball on touch. Jump over them.

26.name: Hidden exit
26.note: A colourless exit that appears once every key is collected. It leads to the world's hidden level.

28.name: Arrow
28.note: A square the ball can only leave in the direction the arrow points.

29.name: Start on a clock
29.note: The block and face the ball starts the level on. Here it is a clock rather than a plain square.

30.name: Start
30.note: The block and face the ball starts the level on.

31.name: Key
31.note: Collecting every key on a level opens the exit, which turns from red to green.

32.name: Lethargy pill
32.note: Slows the ball, rocks the screen and runs the timer fast for three seconds. That costs about fifteen extra seconds on the clock.

33.name: Bouncy pill
33.note: Makes every forward move a two-square bounce and a jump three, until the level ends.

34.name: Invincibility pill
34.note: Makes the ball invincible for fourteen seconds, flashing in colours while it lasts. No hazard harms it, and it cancels the lethargy and bouncy pills. Only on the object catalogue level, so nothing in play uses it.

35.name: Hourglass
35.note: Flips the timer, and scores more the less time is left when you take it. It scores 1200 − 12 × (seconds left), rounded to the nearest 10.

36.name: Gem
36.note: Blue, green or red, and worth the same whatever the colour.

37.name: Coin
37.note: Three tiers, told apart by colour. Bronze is worth 250, blue 500 and gold 750.

38.name: Sunglasses
38.note: Reveals invisible blocks for a while.

42.note: A many-pointed star that turns from brown to green and back every few seconds. While brown it captures the ball on touch, and while green it can be collected for 1550. Only on the object catalogue level, so nothing in play uses it.

43.name: Fruit
43.note: Apple, watermelon, pumpkin, bananas and strawberry come round in turn. Collecting all five earns a bonus level.

44.name: Fruit
44.note: Apple, watermelon, pumpkin, bananas and strawberry come round in turn. Collecting all five earns a bonus level.

45.name: Fruit
45.note: Apple, watermelon, pumpkin, bananas and strawberry come round in turn. Collecting all five earns a bonus level.

46.name: Fruit
46.note: Apple, watermelon, pumpkin, bananas and strawberry come round in turn. Collecting all five earns a bonus level.

47.name: Fruit
47.note: Apple, watermelon, pumpkin, bananas and strawberry come round in turn. Collecting all five earns a bonus level.

50.name: Captivator
50.note: A spiked star that captures the ball on touch. It is the thinner one, with three long points. It travels the space it has and turns back at any wall or object in its way.

51.name: Rolling stone
51.note: A grey cylinder that rolls slowly round a set course and captures the ball on touch. It can be jumped over.

52.name: Captivator
52.note: A spiked star that captures the ball on touch. It is the fuller one, with four short points. It slides back and forth over a fixed stretch, as if on a spring.

53.name: Captivator, wandering
53.note: A blue hexagonal ball that captures yours on touch. It shakes, then moves one square, and the way it shakes gives away where it is going. Its walk looks random, but it starts out the same way every time the level begins.

56.name: Captivator, bouncing
56.note: A corkscrew that bounces up and down and captures the ball on touch. Roll under it when it is up, and jump it when it is down.

/HIRO/HIRO.PAK#19.note: The training level the Japanese release lists as Lesson on its main menu, with one of nearly everything the game has on one floor. The other two releases keep it on the disc but off the menu.

/HILLS/HILLS.PAK#15.note: The level holds 3500 more points, in the twelve coins on the corners of the lowest ring. They and the four gems inside that ring cannot both be had, and the gems score more. The Japanese release removes the coins.

/HILLS/HILLS.PAK#18.note: The best known score, and not a certain one. It takes the coin under the exit block, which the Japanese release removes as unreachable. It leaves one of the ten crumbling blocks, the 50 more points the level holds.

/HILLS/HILLS.PAK#19.note: The developers' object catalogue, with one of nearly every object in the game laid out on a flat floor. It ships unchanged in nine of the ten worlds, and nothing in the game leads to it.

/HILLS/HILLSFI.PAK#0.note: The Final has no fruit, but the PAL release put an apple on this level anyway. The US and Japanese releases removed it, leaving the blue teleporter it stood beside with nothing to reach.

/INCA/INCA.PAK#9.note: The level holds 100 more points, two crumbling blocks that cannot be reached.

/INCA/INCA.PAK#19.note: The developers' object catalogue, with one of nearly every object in the game laid out on a flat floor. It ships unchanged in nine of the ten worlds, and nothing in the game leads to it.

/FIELD/FIELD.PAK#7.note: The level holds 150 more points, three crumbling blocks on the top level that cannot be broken by any means.

/FIELD/FIELD.PAK#15.note: The Japanese release redesigned this level, taking out the gem ringed with spike traps. This is the US layout.

/FIELD/FIELD.PAK#16.note: The level holds 4475 more points, in the gem and two gold coins on whichever end block is reached last. Touching the last block ends a bonus level before anything on it can be collected. The Japanese release puts a single gem on each end instead.

/FIELD/FIELD.PAK#18.note: The Japanese release took a coin and the two moving platforms out of this level. The platforms made the coin easier to reach and back from, and were not the only way.

/FIELD/FIELD.PAK#19.note: The developers' object catalogue, with one of nearly every object in the game laid out on a flat floor. It ships unchanged in nine of the ten worlds, and nothing in the game leads to it.

/FIELD/FIELDFI.PAK#1.note: The level holds 50 more points, a crumbling block that cannot be reached.

/ATLANT/ATLANT.PAK#3.note: The level holds 50 more points, a crumbling block that is out of reach.

/ATLANT/ATLANT.PAK#11.note: The level holds 750 more points, in a gold coin inside one of the rings that cannot be reached. The Japanese release removes it.

/ATLANT/ATLANT.PAK#19.note: The developers' object catalogue, with one of nearly every object in the game laid out on a flat floor. It ships unchanged in nine of the ten worlds, and nothing in the game leads to it.

/ATLANT/ATLANTFI.PAK#0.note: The level holds 200 more points, four of the fifteen crumbling blocks, which the best score leaves standing.

/HAZE/HAZE.PAK#19.note: The developers' object catalogue, with one of nearly every object in the game laid out on a flat floor. It ships unchanged in nine of the ten worlds, and nothing in the game leads to it.

/HAZE/HAZEFI.PAK#1.note: The level holds 30500 more points. That is ten of the eleven gems on the ring at y=28, which cannot be left once reached, and a gold coin.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#7.note: The level holds 100 more points, two of the five crumbling blocks, which the best score leaves standing.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#10.note: The Japanese release un-iced one face of the solid ice block for an arrow that nothing can reach. It also removed the blue coin on the same block, which can be collected here.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#11.note: The hidden exit at 14,19,18 stands on a block that cannot be reached once it has appeared. The PAL release forgot to place it, and the Japanese release moved it to LEVEL 134, the one release in which every hidden level can be played.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#12.note: The Japanese release moved one of the gems off the lethal tile it stands on here onto a kinder one.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#13.note: The Japanese release moves the world's hidden exit to this level.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#16.note: The level holds 8925 more points, in three gems under the three far blocks. Only the bouncy pill reaches them, and the pill then keeps you from collecting them. The Japanese release removes them.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#18.note: The only hidden level with a fruit, at 9,18,15, which the Japanese release removed. In this release the exit that leads here is out of reach.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#19.note: The developers' object catalogue, with one of nearly every object in the game laid out on a flat floor. It ships unchanged in nine of the ten worlds, and nothing in the game leads to it.

/HELL/HELL.PAK#14.note: The level holds 50 more points, one crumbling block that the best score leaves standing.

/HELL/HELL.PAK#15.note: The level holds 1000 more points, in the two coins on top of the first platform, a face that cannot be reached. The Japanese release removes them.

/HELL/HELL.PAK#16.note: The level holds 750 more points, and what the best score leaves out is not known.

/HELL/HELL.PAK#17.note: The level holds 250 more points, and what the best score leaves out is not known. This is the one arcade level rebuilt between the PAL and the US release.

/HELL/HELL.PAK#18.note: 160 of its 178 blocks are not part of the level. They lie flat far below it, spelling VERY WELL DONE in block letters six blocks tall. The other 18 are an upright frame, and everything on the level stands on the side from which the lettering reads the right way round.

/HELL/HELL.PAK#19.note: The developers' object catalogue, with one of nearly every object in the game laid out on a flat floor. It ships unchanged in nine of the ten worlds, and nothing in the game leads to it.
